# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1090

## Korean source

```text
  1|1090화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|
  6|청해성은 엄연히 변방(邊防)에 속하는 지역이다.
  7|
  8|천하에서 손에 꼽힐 정도의 광활한 면적과 아름다운 경관을 지녔지만, 물자의 풍부함과 가호(家戶)의 숫자는 중원에 비해 턱없이 부족한 것이 현실.
  9|
 10|그렇기에 누천년에 걸쳐 천하의 중심으로 자리매김하며 다방면의 문물(文物)을 발전시킨 중원과 비교될 때마다, 청해성의 사람들은 농담 삼아 이렇게 자평하고는 했다.
 11|
 12|― 청해와 중원의 공통점은 오직 세 가지뿐이다. 같은 해를 보고, 같은 물(황하黃河)로 이어져 있고, 마지막으로 거지가 있다.
 13|
 14|거지는 그만큼 어느 곳에서나 흔해 빠진 존재들이었다.
 15|
 16|시끌벅적한 대로변이나 어둡고 지저분한 뒷골목, 혹은 개울가 근처의 움막촌 따위에서 살아가는 그들은 중원이든 변방이든 가리지 않았다.
 17|
 18|그 머릿수가 얼마나 많은지, 천하의 모든 거지를 개방이 흡수한다면 능히 일국(一國)을 세울 수도 있다는 우스갯소리가 나올 정도니까.
 19|
 20|하지만 서서히 동이 틀 무렵, 어스름한 새벽안개를 뚫고 주위를 탐색하던 정찰대에 의해 발견된 어느 백발의 거지는 지금껏 누구도 본 적 없는 행색을 하고 있었다.
 21|
 22|아니, 솜털이 곤두설 만큼 낯설었다.
 23|
 24|터벅, 터벅.
 25|
 26|당장이라도 쓰러질 듯이 비틀거리는 발걸음. 혼백이 빠져나간 것처럼 공허한 눈동자.
 27|
 28|그리고…….
 29|
 30|“전해라. 반드시. 누가 살아남든.”
 31|
 32|파랗게 질린 입술 사이로 흘러나오는 공포 어린 목소리.
 33|
 34|아마도 그래서였을 것이다.
 35|
 36|찰나의 순간, 석상처럼 굳어 있던 정찰대가 뒤늦게 거지의 허리춤에 묶인 두 개의 매듭을 발견한 것은.
 37|
 38|“……개방(丐幇).”
 39|
 40|틀림없다. 눈앞의 저 거지는 개방에 몸담은 무림인이었다.
 41|
 42|그것도 분타주 바로 아랫급의 이결제자.
 43|
 44|그리고 정찰대가 출발한 서녕으로부터 서쪽에서 백 리나 떨어진 이곳에서 개방도가 모습을 드러낼 이유는, 그들이 알기로 단 한 가지 경우밖에 없었다.
 45|
 46|“노인장, 도대체 청해호에서 무슨 일이 있었……!”
 47|
 48|그 순간. 다급히 말에서 내려 다가가던 정찰대원이 헛숨을 삼키며 눈을 부릅떴다.
 49|
 50|그제야 보았기 때문이다.
 51|
 52|희끄무레한 안개 속에서는 그저 노화로 인한 백발로 보였던 개방도의 머리카락이, 사실은 빙하에 갇혀 있던 사람처럼 얼어 붙어 있었음을.
 53|
 54|새하얗게 물든 그의 얼굴은 노인이 아닌 청년에 불과했음을.
 55|
 56|“이, 이게 무슨.”
 57|
 58|한 줄기의 벼락이 정수리를 관통한다면 이런 기분일까.
 59|
 60|스무 명의 정찰대는 찌르르 울리는 등골을 느끼며 침묵할 수밖에 없었다.
 61|
 62|바로 다음 순간 들려온 개방도의 한 마디가, 그가 혼신을 다한 마지막 불꽃이라는 사실조차 알지 못한 채.
 63|
 64|“전해라. 내가 갈 것이다. 가서, 서녕의 모든 것을 죽이고 불태울 것이다.”
 65|
 66|“……!”
 67|
 68|“……!”
 69|
 70|일순간, 정찰대는 경악에 찬 눈빛으로 몸을 떨었다.
 71|
 72|그 말에 담긴 무시무시한 살의(殺意) 때문에?
 73|
 74|아니다. 틀렸다.
 75|
 76|개방도.
 77|
 78|그는 웃고 있었다. 동시에 울고 있었다.
 79|
 80|마치 이 말을 전하라고 명령한 누군가를 따라 하듯이.
 81|
 82|그와 더불어 이미 불귀의 객이 되어 버린 동료들의 죽음을 슬퍼하듯이.
 83|
 84|그리고 온 사방을 짓누르는 그 숨 막히는 침묵 속, 힘겨운 여정을 끝마친 개방도의 몸뚱어리가 흐릿한 목소리와 함께 기울어졌다.
 85|
 86|“기다려라. 내가, 혈주(血主)가 돌아 왔…….”
 87|
 88|쿵.
 89|
 90|썩은 통나무처럼 허물어지는 육신.
 91|
 92|아니, 마침내 숨이 끊어진 개방도의 시신을 멍하니 바라보던 정찰대원들은 불현듯 고개를 들어 서쪽을 바라보았다.
 93|
 94|어째서일까.
 95|
 96|이미 마음속에서 싹 튼 두려움 때문일까, 아니면 곧 마주하게 될 현실을 깨달은 본능적인 직감일까.
 97|
 98|저 자욱한 안개 너머에서 끔찍한 괴물들이 내지르는 괴성과 악취가 풍겨오는 듯했다.
 99|
100|“……시신을 수습해라.”
101|
102|간신히 쥐어 짜낸 상관의 목소리에서조차 숨길 수 없는 공포가 묻어나왔다.
103|
104|“서녕으로 돌아간다. 지금 당장.”
105|
106|
107|
108|* * *
109|
110|
111|
112|이제는 목 없는 시체가 되어 버린 청해성주의 집무실은 언제 보아도 이루 말할 데 없이 넓고 호화로웠다.
113|
114|그가 죽을 수밖에 없었던 이유를 증명하기라도 하는 것처럼.
115|
116|값비싼 흑단(黑檀)을 깎아 만든 탁자는 수십여 명이 동시에 자리할 만큼 컸고, 사천에서도 특등품 취급받는 촉금(蜀錦) 비단을 햇빛을 가리기 위한 용도로 썼을 정도였다.
117|
118|하지만 청해성주는 까맣게 몰랐을 것이다.
119|
120|그가 죽기 직전까지도 아까워했을 그 요란한 사치품들이, 지금 이 순간 어느 초라한 거지를 위해 쓰이고 있다는 것을.
121|
122|“이결제자 주제에 이런 호사라니. 거지의 본분을 잊었군.”
123|
124|궁기방은 애써 담담한 목소리로 뇌까렸다.
125|
126|촉금 비단에 감싸 인 채, 흑단 탁자 위에 올려진 시신을 바라보는 녀석의 눈빛은 축축하게 젖어 있었다.
127|
128|“그리 오래 알았던 건 아니지만 썩 괜찮은 녀석이었어. 아직 어린 나이인데도 이결을 허락받을 만큼의 재능도 있었고.”
129|
130|나는 대답하지 않았다.
131|
132|아니, 나뿐만 아니라 집무실 안에 모여있던 수뇌부 중 그 누구도.
133|
134|“상황이 괜찮아지면 나중에라도 중원에 꼭 한번 가 보고 싶다고 부탁하길래, 철없는 소리 하지 말라고 역정을 냈었는데……. 제기랄.”
135|
136|먹먹한 목소리로 욕설을 내뱉은 궁기방이 쓴웃음을 지었다.
137|
138|“어쩌겠어. 단지 운이 없었던 거지. 이 녀석도, 그들도.”
139|
140|삼십여 명에 가까운 개방도가 청해호 건너편에 남았지만, 서녕으로 돌아올 수 있었던 것은 저 이름 모를 젊은 개방도 하나뿐이다.
141|
142|그리고 그마저도 도중에 숨이 끊어졌다.
143|
144|가장 먼저 그를 발견한 정찰대들이 제대로 말을 잇지 못할 만큼 처참한 모습으로.
145|
146|하지만 유언(遺言)이나 다름없게 된 그의 마지막 한 마디에는, 이 빌어먹게 호화로운 집무실 전체보다 값진 정보가 담겨 있었다.
147|
148|“혈주. 혈주라면…….”
149|
150|불현듯 입을 연 곤륜파의 장문인, 청허자(淸虛子)의 뇌까림에 내가 고개를 끄덕였다.
151|
152|“장문인께서 알고 계시는 그 이름이 맞습니다. 소림혈사(小林血史)를 일으켰던.”
153|
154|“……!”
155|
156|“……!”
157|
158|보이지 않는 파동이 주위로 번진다.
159|
160|이미 전부터 혈주의 존재를 알고 있던 이들은 말없이 침음성만 흘렸고, 자세한 정황을 몰랐던 이들은 놀라서 눈을 부릅떴다.
161|
162|그리고 화왕 적천강은, 그 어디에도 속하지 않은 극소수의 인물 중 하나였다.
163|
164|“그리웠던 이름이군.”
165|
166|나직한 음성과 별다른 변화가 보이지 않는 표정.
167|
168|그러나 나는 누구보다 잘 알고 있다.
169|
170|지금 이 순간 적천강이 얼마나 분노하고 있는지.
171|
172|동시에 그 분노를 억누르기 위해 얼마나 안간힘을 쓰고 있는지.
173|
174|“이제야 그 땡중에게 면이 설 수 있겠어.”
175|
176|무림의 태산북두라 불리는 소림사의 방장이자, 법왕(法王)이라는 별호를 얻을 만큼 신망이 두텁던 굉도였지만 적천강은 그를 늘 땡중이라고 불렀다.
177|
178|일생을 통틀어 몇 안 되는. 아니, 어쩌면 하나밖에 없었을지도 모르는 친우였으니까.
179|
180|그렇기에 지금껏 단 한 순간도 잊지 않았을 것이다.
181|
182|그런 굉도를 죽인 장본인, 혈주에 대한 원한을.
183|
184|하지만 지금은 그의 원한보다 중요한 문제가 남아 있었다.
185|
186|“결국 놈들로서도 총력전을 벌일 심산이군요.”
187|
188|냉정하게 느껴질 만큼 침착한 목소리로 입을 연 젊은 도사, 청허자의 둘째 제자인 학의(鶴義)가 말을 이었다.
189|
190|“이미 사로잡은 개방도를 구태여 풀어 주었다는 건, 그만큼 승리를 확신한다는 뜻일 테고요.”
191|
192|“두, 둘째야.”
193|
194|그와는 달리 옆자리에서 눈치를 보던 사형, 학수(學洙)가 만류하려 했지만 학의는 개의치 않았다.
195|
196|청해성주에 관련된 지난번 회의 이후 어느 정도의 발언권을 얻게 된 그였다.
197|
198|“하지만 가장 중요한 정보를 전달받지 못한 것이 아쉽습니다. 적들의 숫자만이라도 알 수 있었다면 훨씬 더 나은 대책을…….”
199|
200|바로 그 순간이었다.
201|
202|“뭐?”
203|
204|그때까지도 말없이 시신만을 바라보던 궁기방의 미간이 와락 일그러진 것은.
205|
206|“지금, 뭐라고 했소?”
207|
208|분노를 내비치는 궁기방을 향해, 학의가 담담한 어투로 대꾸했다.
209|
210|“단지 아쉬움에 제 생각을 말씀드린 것뿐입니다.”
211|
212|“그래서? 모두를 위해 위험을 무릅쓰다 죽은 사람에게 책임을 묻겠다는 건가? 왜 더 노력하지 않았느냐고?”
213|
214|“그건…….”
215|
216|감정이 격해진 궁기방의 모습에 학의가 뭐라 답하려던 그때, 조용히 사태를 지켜보던 한 사람이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
217|
218|“둘째야.”
219|
220|다름 아닌 스승, 청허자다.
221|
222|그의 나직한 부름에 멈칫한 학의가 이내 궁기방을 향해 고개를 숙였다.
223|
224|“제가 미숙한 탓에 그만 실언을 했습니다. 더 이상의 오해는 없었으면 합니다.”
225|
226|별다른 감정이 느껴지지 않는 그 딱딱한 사죄에 궁기방의 표정이 더욱 험악해진 그때, 청허자가 재차 입을 열었다.
227|
228|“빈도가 제자를 잘못 키웠네. 진심을 다해 사과하지.”
229|
230|다른 사람도 아니고 한참 대선배, 그것도 곤륜파의 장문인이 직접 건네는 사과다.
231|
232|뿐인가.
233|
234|지금 이 자리에는 그보다 높은 이들도 있다.
235|
236|궁기방이 아무리 개방의 후개라도 해도 더 이상의 분란은 엄청난 무례로 여겨질 수 있는 상황.
237|
238|입술을 질끈 깨무는 녀석과 학의를 물끄러미 응시하던 나는 때맞춰 전음(傳音)을 흘려보냈다.
239|
240|― 넘어가자, 우선은.
241|
242|“……!”
243|
244|― 아니면 내가 지금 당장 저 사회 부적응자 새끼를 반쯤 죽여 줄 수도 있고. 뭐가 더 나은지 말만 해.
245|
246|그제야 쓴웃음을 흘린 궁기방이 고개를 절레절레 저었다.
247|
248|“알겠습니다. 저도 괜히 분위기를 흐려서 죄송합니다.”
249|
250|그렇게 잠깐의 소란이 일단락되었지만, 학의는 조금도 움츠러든 기색 없이 입을 열었다.
251|
252|“다행히 적들이 서녕에 도달하기까지는 아직 시간이 남아 있습니다. 그 안에 충분한 대비책을 마련해야겠지요.”
253|
254|어째서인지 묘한 어투다.
255|
256|깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 줄곧 그를 주시하던 나도 이제는 묻지 않을 수 없었다.
257|
258|“뭡니까. 그 대비책이?”
259|
260|“진 대협께서도 이미 알고 계시지 않습니까.”
261|
262|물론 안다. 너무 잘 알아서 문제다.
263|
264|그래서 더욱 놀라웠다.
265|
266|눈앞의 학의가, 곤륜파의 도맥(道脈)을 이은 그가 그런 생각을 했다는 것이.
267|
268|“지금이라도 늦지 않았습니다. 후방이 완전히 가로막히기 전에 당장 이곳을 떠나야 합니다.”
269|

[P101]
His Master, Cheongheoja.

[P102]
Hak Eui paused at the quiet call, then bowed his head to Gung Gibang.

[P103]
“I spoke carelessly because I’m inexperienced. I hope there will be no further misunderstanding.”

[P104]
There was little feeling in the stiff apology. Gung Gibang’s expression darkened further, but Cheongheoja spoke again.

[P105]
“I failed to raise my Disciple properly. I sincerely apologize.”

[P106]
This was no ordinary apology. It came from a far more senior martial artist, and the Sect Leader of the Kunlun Sect at that.

[P107]
There were others present who outranked even him.

[P108]
No matter that Gung Gibang was the Beggars’ Sect Successor Beggar, prolonging the argument now could be seen as a grave act of disrespect.

[P109]
I watched him bite his lip, then looked at Hak Eui. At the right moment, I sent Gung Gibang a Sound Transmission.

[P110]
*—Let it go. For now.*

[P111]
“…!”

[P112]
*—Or I can beat that socially maladjusted bastard half to death right now. Just tell me which you’d prefer.*

[P113]
At last, Gung Gibang gave a bitter smile and shook his head.

[P114]
“Understood. I’m sorry for souring the mood, too.”

[P115]
That brought the brief commotion to an end. Hak Eui spoke again, without the slightest sign of having been cowed.

[P116]
“Fortunately, we still have time before the enemy reaches Xining. We need to make adequate preparations before then.”

[P117]
There was something odd about his tone.

[P118]
I’d been watching him closely. Now I couldn’t help asking.

[P119]
“What preparations?”

[P120]
“You already know, Great Hero Jin.”

[P121]
Of course I did. I knew all too well.

[P122]
That was what made it so surprising—that Hak Eui, heir to the Kunlun Sect’s Daoist lineage, would suggest it.

[P123]
“It’s not too late. We must leave this place at once, before the route behind us is completely cut off.”

[P124]
“Junior Brother, what are you saying?”

[P125]
Hak Su sprang to his feet, unable to hold back any longer. Even Cheongheoja let out a troubled murmur. Hak Eui still didn’t stop.

[P126]
“This isn’t a battle. It’s a war. I know it isn’t right to say this, but… we can’t make the mistake of clinging to something small and losing everything.”

[P127]
“…!”

[P128]
“…!”

[P129]
The air in the room froze.

[P130]
Then I spoke.

[P131]
“Uh, first of all, there’s too much bullshit there to answer point by point. So let’s start with this.”

[P132]
I looked at Hak Eui’s rigid face and added quietly.

[P133]
“Does the Blood Lord look like a pushover to you?”

[P134]
I pointed at the table.

[P135]
More precisely, at the Beggars’ Sect disciple’s corpse, lying there with frost on patches of his body.

[P136]
I’d known from the moment I first saw him.

[P137]
That terrible cold still lingering in his dead body. I recognized its familiar trace—one only I could detect.

[P138]
*Blizzard.*

[P139]
A highest-tier ice spell with devastating power.

[P140]
It meant two things.

[P141]
First, just as I’d expected, the Grand Mage was with them.

[P142]
And second—

[P143]
“They’ve already crossed Qinghai Lake.”

[P144]
They wouldn’t have needed boats. They could simply walk across the lake, frozen solid by magic.

[P145]
The Blood Lord had only released the Beggars’ Sect disciple for his own amusement in the first place.

[P146]
“So,” I said quietly to Hak Eui, whose expression I couldn’t read, “if you want to run, leave now. You cowardly bastard.”

[P147]
And at that moment—

[P148]
Rrrk. Rrrrrk.

[P149]
A tremor came from somewhere, and the office began to shake.

[P150]
No—the whole of Xining.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

All twenty scouts fell silent, a chill running down their spines.

[P29]
They had no idea that the disciple’s next words would be the last spark of his life, spoken with every ounce of strength he had left.

[P30]
“Tell them. I’m coming. I’ll go to Xining and kill and burn everything there.”

[P31]
“…!”

[P32]
“…!”

[P33]
The scouts trembled, their eyes wide with shock.

[P34]
Because of the terrifying killing intent in those words?

[P35]
No. That wasn’t it.

[P36]
The Beggars’ Sect disciple was smiling. And crying at the same time.

[P37]
As though imitating whoever had ordered him to deliver the message.

[P38]
As though grieving for the comrades who were already dead.

[P39]
Then, in the suffocating silence that pressed down on them all, his body tilted. His difficult journey had come to an end.

[P40]
“Wait for me. I, the Blood Lord, have returned…”

[P41]
Thud.

[P42]
His body crumpled like a rotten log.

[P43]
The scouts stared blankly at the Beggars’ Sect disciple’s corpse. Then, all at once, they raised their heads and looked west.

[P44]
Why?

[P45]
Was it the fear already taking root in their hearts, or an instinctive sense of what they were about to face?

[P46]
Beyond the thick mist, they could almost hear the shrieks of hideous monsters and smell their stench.

[P47]
“…See to his body.”

[P48]
The commander had to force the words out, and even then his voice couldn’t hide his fear.

[P49]
“We’re going back to Xining. Right now.”

[P50]
* * *

[P51]
The office of the Qinghai City Lord—now a headless corpse—was as impossibly spacious and luxurious as ever.

[P52]
As though it existed to prove why he’d had to die.

[P53]
Its expensive ebony table was large enough to seat dozens of people at once. He had even used Shu brocade, prized as a first-rate luxury in Sichuan, to keep out the sunlight.

[P54]
But the City Lord could never have known that the gaudy luxuries he’d treasured until his death would now be put to use for a shabby beggar.

[P55]
“Enjoying this kind of luxury when you’re only a two-knot disciple. You forgot what it means to be a beggar.”

[P56]
Gung Gibang muttered, doing his best to sound calm.

[P57]
The corpse lay on the ebony table, wrapped in Shu brocade. Gung Gibang’s eyes glistened as he looked at it.

[P58]
“I didn’t know him long, but he was a good kid. Still young, and already talented enough to be granted the second knot.”

[P59]
I said nothing.

[P60]
Neither did any of the other leaders gathered in the office.

[P61]
“He asked if he could visit the Central Plains someday, once things got better. I snapped at him for saying something so childish… Damn it.”

[P62]
Gung Gibang swore in a hollow voice and gave a bitter smile.

[P63]
“What can you do? He and the others were just unlucky.”

[P64]
Nearly thirty Beggars’ Sect disciples had stayed on the far side of Qinghai Lake. Only one young disciple whose name I didn’t know had made it back toward Xining.

[P65]
And even he had died along the way.

[P66]
He’d been in such a terrible state that the scouts who found him could barely speak.

[P67]
But his final words, almost a dying message, contained information more valuable than everything in this goddamn luxurious office.

[P68]
“The Blood Lord. If it’s the Blood Lord…”

[P69]
I nodded at the murmur from Cheongheoja, the Kunlun Sect Leader.

[P70]
“It’s the same one you’re thinking of, Sect Leader. The one behind the Shaolin Bloodshed.”

[P71]
“…!”

[P72]
“…!”

[P73]
An invisible ripple passed through the room.

[P74]
Those who already knew of the Blood Lord let out low murmurs without a word. Those who hadn’t known the details stared in shock.

[P75]
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, belonged to neither group.

[P76]
“A name I’ve longed to hear again.”

[P77]
His voice was quiet, his expression barely changed.

[P78]
But I knew better than anyone how furious Jeok Cheongang was.

[P79]
And how hard he was fighting to hold that fury back.

[P80]
“Now I can hold my head up in front of that damned monk.”

[P81]
Hong Dao had been the Abbot of Shaolin Temple, known as the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and respected enough to earn the title of Dharma King. Yet Jeok Cheongang had always called him “that damned monk.”

[P82]
He’d been one of the very few friends Jeok Cheongang had ever had. Maybe the only one.

[P83]
There was no way Jeok Cheongang had forgotten, even for a moment, his grudge against the man who had killed Hong Dao.

[P84]
But right now, there was something more pressing than his grudge.

[P85]
“So they mean to throw everything they have into this after all.”

[P86]
A young Daoist spoke in a voice so calm it almost sounded cold. Hak Eui, Cheongheoja’s second Disciple, continued.

[P87]
“They went to the trouble of releasing a Beggars’ Sect disciple they’d already captured. That must mean they’re certain they’ll win.”

[P88]
“S-second brother.”

[P89]
Hak Su, his Senior Brother, had been watching the room uneasily and tried to stop him. Hak Eui paid him no mind.

[P90]
He’d gained a measure of influence since the last meeting about the Qinghai City Lord.

[P91]
“But it’s unfortunate we didn’t receive the most important information. If we’d known even the enemy’s numbers, we could have made a much better plan—”

[P92]
“What?”

[P93]
Gung Gibang, who had been staring at the corpse in silence, suddenly scowled.

[P94]
“What did you just say?”

[P95]
Hak Eui answered his anger evenly.

[P96]
“I was only expressing my regret.”

[P97]
“So what? Are you blaming a man who risked his life for everyone and died? Asking why he didn’t try harder?”

[P98]
“That’s…”

[P99]
Hak Eui was about to respond when someone who had been watching quietly spoke up.

[P100]
“Second.”

[P101]
His Master, Cheongheoja.

[P102]
Hak Eui paused at the quiet call, then bowed his head to Gung Gibang.

[P103]
“I spoke carelessly because I’m inexperienced. I hope there will be no further misunderstanding.”

[P104]
There was little feeling in the stiff apology. Gung Gibang’s expression darkened further, but Cheongheoja spoke again.

[P105]
“I failed to raise my Disciple properly. I sincerely apologize.”

[P106]
This was no ordinary apology. It came from a far more senior martial artist, and the Sect Leader of the Kunlun Sect at that.

[P107]
There were others present who outranked even him.

[P108]
No matter that Gung Gibang was the Beggars’ Sect Successor Beggar, prolonging the argument now could be seen as a grave act of disrespect.

[P109]
I watched him bite his lip, then looked at Hak Eui. At the right moment, I sent Gung Gibang a Sound Transmission.

[P110]
*—Let it go. For now.*

[P111]
“…!”

[P112]
*—Or I can beat that socially maladjusted bastard half to death right now. Just tell me which you’d prefer.*

[P113]
At last, Gung Gibang gave a bitter smile and shook his head.

[P114]
“Understood. I’m sorry for souring the mood, too.”

[P115]
That brought the brief commotion to an end. Hak Eui spoke again, without the slightest sign of having been cowed.

[P116]
“Fortunately, we still have time before the enemy reaches Xining. We need to make adequate preparations before then.”

[P117]
There was something odd about his tone.

[P118]
I’d been watching him closely. Now I couldn’t help asking.

[P119]
“What preparations?”

[P120]
“You already know, Great Hero Jin.”

[P121]
Of course I did. I knew all too well.

[P122]
That was what made it so surprising—that Hak Eui, heir to the Kunlun Sect’s Daoist lineage, would suggest it.

[P123]
“It’s not too late. We must leave this place at once, before the route behind us is completely cut off.”

[P124]
“Junior Brother, what are you saying?”

[P125]
Hak Su sprang to his feet, unable to hold back any longer. Even Cheongheoja let out a troubled murmur. Hak Eui still didn’t stop.

[P126]
“This isn’t a battle. It’s a war. I know it isn’t right to say this, but… we can’t make the mistake of clinging to something small and losing everything.”

[P127]
“…!”

[P128]
“…!”

[P129]
The air in the room froze.

[P130]
Then I spoke.

[P131]
“Uh, first of all, there’s too much bullshit there to answer point by point. So let’s start with this.”

[P132]
I looked at Hak Eui’s rigid face and added quietly.

[P133]
“Does the Blood Lord look like a pushover to you?”

[P134]
I pointed at the table.

[P135]
More precisely, at the Beggars’ Sect disciple’s corpse, lying there with frost on patches of his body.

[P136]
I’d known from the moment I first saw him.

[P137]
That terrible cold still lingering in his dead body. I recognized its familiar trace—one only I could detect.

[P138]
*Blizzard.*

[P139]
A highest-tier ice spell with devastating power.

[P140]
It meant two things.

[P141]
First, just as I’d expected, the Grand Mage was with them.

[P142]
And second—

[P143]
“They’ve already crossed Qinghai Lake.”

[P144]
They wouldn’t have needed boats. They could simply walk across the lake, frozen solid by magic.

[P145]
The Blood Lord had only released the Beggars’ Sect disciple for his own amusement in the first place.

[P146]
“So,” I said quietly to Hak Eui, whose expression I couldn’t read, “if you want to run, leave now. You cowardly bastard.”

[P147]
And at that moment—

[P148]
Rrrk. Rrrrrk.

[P149]
A tremor came from somewhere, and the office began to shake.

[P150]
No—the whole of Xining.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
